ending.E1.text:
You lift the gold ink and trace Ashenport back into the Weave, stroke by stroke.
The faded street names come back, the house plates come back, and someone finishes the sums in the empty classroom. But the rule of re-inking doesn't change: every stroke is paid for by someone.
One by one the scribes' names fade, like shells handed back by the ebb. At dawn no one in the plaza remembers the rain — except you, and the codex in your arms that keeps growing fuller.
The city is saved. The blank stays with the ones who saved it.
ending.E2.text:
You throw the last page into the fire.
The moment the Weave lets go, Ashenport sways gently — and then, for the first time, stands on its own. The Fading stops: no one is revoked any more, and no one is written back in.
Freedom is grey: names will age, ink will fade, and the city will grow old, slowly and honestly.
The Uninked's black feathers circle above the fire. From now on, every page has to be written by hand.
ending.E3.text:
In your palm, the four fragments come together into the outline of a pen. Kelan smooths the paper flat for you.
You don't mend it, and you don't burn it — you turn the Weave over, and where everyone thought the story ended, you write the first line: "Ashenport, continued."
Where the ink lands, the revocation begins to run backwards. A ruined book can be given a fresh sheet — a rule the Weavers left behind that no one ever dared to use.
From today, the Unwritten are blank no longer. You are the Penbearer.
ending.E4.text:
In the end, you never set pen to the last page.
The blank at the top of the tower spills down over the plaza, the harbor and the mudflats where you first woke, and turns Ashenport over — gently, completely.
You leave carrying scraps of the codex. There are no ruins behind you — ruins are a kind of writing too, and here even the ruins have been erased.
Failure is not the end: the scraps remember everything. In the tide of your next playthrough, you'll see more clearly.
endings.E1.content: The city is rewritten, but those who paid for it stay blank forever.

endings.E1.text_variants.0.text: The memory you gave away is among them. The gold ink traced back other people's streets; your own page stays forever on a clean, blank white.

lore.ashenport_local_01:
Fog Wharf was once Ashenport's first harbor; the tide table was carved into the breakwater, every word visible at low tide.
Today the stone has worn half away and the tides keep no schedule — only those with the old chart know when the secret passage opens.
lore.ashenport_local_01.title: Ashenport Gazetteer · Fog Wharf
lore.revoked_registry_01:
On the house plate you can just make out: "No. 11, Fog Wharf. The name changes with the tide; the people stay with the lamp."
On the back, a row of small tally marks, stopping at the seven hundred and thirty-first stroke.
lore.revoked_registry_01.title: The Faded Dwelling's House Plate
lore.revoked_registry_02:
Thirty-seven names on the class roll, and thirty-six have faded to their first stroke.
Beside the one clear name, a note in the child's own hand: "I remember me."
lore.revoked_registry_02.title: The Empty Classroom's Roll
lore.weaver_fragment_01:
"When the words begin to fade, it starts with water. Do not hold them with gold ink by force — what is held by force is primed with memory."
The fragment's edge is scorched, as if someone wanted to destroy it and couldn't bring themselves to.
lore.weaver_fragment_01.title: Fragment · I
lore.weaver_fragment_02:
"The Weave is no cage but a covenant. Lay ten thousand pages one on another, and a city stands. Yet a covenant may have a reverse side —"
The sentence breaks off here; someone turned the back over first.
lore.weaver_fragment_02.title: Fragment · II
lore.weaver_fragment_03:
"I cast the twenty-sided die not to fix fate, but to leave a blank. Wherever there is blank space, all may be rewritten."
On the back of the paper, the shallow print of a die pressed into it.
lore.weaver_fragment_03.title: Fragment · III
lore.weaver_fragment_04:
"To whoever comes after: if you are reading this, the Fading has begun. Do not mend. Do not burn. Turn to the other side."
It isn't signed with a name, but with a blank page.
lore.weaver_fragment_04.source: Carried over from a previous playthrough
lore.weaver_fragment_04.title: Fragment · IV

manifest.name: Ashenport Fragments
node.N0-1.text:
The tide. The taste of salt.
You wake on the mudflats of Ashenport with no codex page in your arms — the page every newborn is given, with a name and a day of death written on it.
The water licks the flats again and again, like a page rewritten over and over. You have nothing. You are one of the Unwritten.
node.N0-2.text:
On a wooden sign nearby, the words "Fog Wharf" are… fading. The strokes drift away like ink washed loose by the sea, leaving the wood one line at a time.
— Focus. This is the first time you cast the Fatedie against the Weave.
node.N0-3a.text:
The instant the Fatedie settles, the Weave leaves you a single blank moment.
You see it clearly: the ink peels away from the sign, rises and dissolves, like a hand drawn back with the ebb.
This is no illusion. The city is being revoked — and you have seen it with your own eyes.
node.N0-3b.text:
You miss the moment of change — but beside you, an old fisherman's pipe falls to the ground.
"Another one… another name gone," he mutters. "First the place names. Then what?"
You help him up and commit his words to memory, for everyone who didn't get to see.
node.N0-4.text:
As you get to your feet, you feel it: across the plaza, three gazes have settled on you.
A grey-robed friar. A black feather under the eaves. A broker from the auction house.
They all know you carry no codex page — and they all know only blank space can take new writing.
node.N1-1.text:
What's left of Ashenport's bustle is crammed into this plaza. Half the city has already been "revoked", and those who remain live with half their memories.
The woman who runs the general store waves you over — word of the Unwritten travels faster than your feet.
Resupply here, listen for rumors, catch your breath. Then go and see the street that is fading.
node.N1-2.text:
The edge of this street looks like pencil worked over with an eraser, fainter the deeper it goes.
You crouch to look for the pattern in how the Fading spreads. In the cracks between the bricks lies a very fine gold dust — something no rumor mentioned.
node.N1-2b.text:
Following the gold dust, you take a wrong turn — and walk straight into a Scriptorium cordon and a pack of Ink Fiends in no mood to talk.
You cut your way out through the ink. The ink waits for no one, and neither does revocation: while you were held up, another page of the city was turned.
node.N1-3.text:
By the time you arrive, the street is disappearing.
Not collapsing, not burning — being "revoked". Houses, flagstones and house plates, along with the glances of passers-by, wiped gently off the page like a typo.
Someone kneels beside you, sobbing out a name — then even the sobbing stops short: he has forgotten whose name he was calling.
node.N1-4.text:
"Unwritten." The grey-robed friar's voice is like turning pages. "The Fading is a rot in the Scroll, and you are the only unspoiled blank. The Scriptorium would like… to borrow you."
He doesn't mention the price. The Scriptorium never writes the price on the first page.
node.N1-5.text:
A black feather lands on your shoulder and unfolds into a line of writing: "Is a life already written worth living? — The Uninked. Midnight. The old lighthouse."
The words burn themselves out the moment you finish reading, and the ash in your palm forms one last stroke: an arrow pointing up.
node.N1-6.text:
"Business people don't waste words." The broker hands you a gilt invitation. "The Fading took half the city, and churned up countless fragments. Fragments are worth money. And a blank that walks around — even more."
In the corner of the card, the Guild's small print: the city's gone, the accounts remain.
node.N1-7.text:
Midnight, and the rain is ink.
Where the drops land they become letters, and the letters twist and stand — Ink Fiends, warped text born of the Fading, surging toward the only blank in the plaza.
When the rain stops, Kelan's hand is still on your shoulder. Tonight you became people written on the same page.
node.N1-8.text:
Before dawn, three offers lie in front of you: the Scriptorium's commission, the Uninked's black feather, the Salvage Guild's contract.
Three pens, three ways of writing. Whichever you take up, Ashenport's next page will lean that way.
node.N2-C.text:
The three lines of intelligence come together on your table into a single map: the Fading doesn't start in the city, but in the Tide Tower — the last page the Weave held in reserve for Ashenport.
The blank at the top of the tower grows every day, a page waiting for someone to write on it, or to tear it out.
It's time to go into the Revoked Quarter, and see the days that have already been "turned over".
node.N2G-1.text:
The auction house is lit brighter than a cathedral. Tonight's final lot is a crate of fragments dredged out of the Revoked Quarter.
The broker whispers prices in your ear while you work out your own price for the broker — talk him round, or pay two hundred gold to keep him quiet.
node.N2G-2.text:
At low tide Fog Wharf looks like an upturned inkwell: wrecks, crates and half-pages of old writing soaking in the shallows.
You feel your way along the waterline inch by inch — only the tide knows which crevice the fragments hide in.
node.N2G-2b.text:
The tide chart didn't lie: at the end of the low-water line, a hidden door lies sunk in a ship's belly.
Behind it is the Sunken Library — a whole library bound into a single volume by the sea, the old borrowers' name tags still hanging from the spines.
In the deepest niche you find a page that belongs to no book: a Weaver's Fragment, its ink older than the sea.
node.N2G-2c.text:
Without the tide chart, you have to go the long way round.
Behind every fork in the fog stands an Ink Fiend, like an ambush typeset in advance.
Every extra step keeps count of the chart you didn't buy.
node.N2G-3.text:
Pieced together, the fragments aren't poetry. They're accounts.
The Guild's private ledger is perfectly clear: three years ago they measured how high the Fading would rise, then stockpiled goods while printing "all is well" in their notices.
Kelan closes the ledger and says nothing for a long time — so the first people to know about the end of the world chose to do business first.
node.N2L-1.text:
Borrowing no one's eyes, you read the city for yourself.
The Fading's course, the three factions' lookouts, the intervals of the midnight ink rain — on your page the clues slowly join into a road no one has walked.
If it holds, you'll be a step ahead of everyone; if it doesn't, three factions' wanted posters will make you famous.
node.N2L-1b.text:
In the end you step right into the spot all three factions had circled.
Scriptorium cordons, Uninked black feathers, Guild enforcers — for once they're working together, and the target is you.
When this fight is over you'll have to pick a side. Ashenport doesn't allow anyone to stay blank forever.
node.N2S-1.text:
The archive's shelves rise out of sight, and every shelf holds a piece of the city's yesterday.
The presiding friar gives you one stick of incense: among a hundred thousand codex pages, find the few the Fading is eating away.
Choose right and the Scriptorium opens its door a crack; choose wrong and time closes it for them.
node.N2S-2.text:
The scribes form a half-circle and lay a faded street corner back down under the gold ink.
The Fading won't allow it. Ink Fiends seep out of the letters and lunge for the writing hand.
Your task comes down to one word: protect — until the last stroke holds.
node.N2S-3.text:
The rite worked. The street corner has a name again, and gold ink glows quietly between the bricks.
The presiding friar slides a ledger across to you: re-inking is not a gift, it is an exchange — the Scriptorium wants a memory of yours to prime the ink.
You think of the man who forgot whose name he was calling. So every word that is remembered means someone, somewhere, forgot something.
Whether or not you agree, the signet is already on the table.
node.N2U-1.text:
Inside the old lighthouse, the black feathers sit in a circle passing round a list torn in half.
You take a seat in the shadows and hold your breath — the Uninked open their door only to those who make no sound.
Listen closely, and you'll learn who tore the first page.
node.N2U-1b.text:
A nail squeals under your boot. Every black feather in the room turns at once.
The Uninked keep no prisoners and respect only fists — if you want to listen in, win your seat first.
node.N2U-2.text:
The operation goes smoothly: the tax collector's page of fate lies open before you, the ink not yet dry.
It records every coin he collected and every revocation order he signed — and his daughter's name.
Tear it, or don't. The Black Feather Token sits on the corner of the table, and the Uninked are waiting for your answer.
node.N2U-3.text:
The next day, the tax collector's name fades from the rolls — or it doesn't. Either way, that night now has consequences.
The Uninked burn every record of the operation and scatter the ash from the top of the lighthouse into the sea, like a small, free snowfall.
Kelan watches the ash and says: so freedom smells of smoke too. You stand there a long time, until the smoke is gone.
node.N3-1.text:
The Revoked Quarter has no gate, only a border that grows fainter and fainter.
Cross it, and sound goes first, then colour — the revoked old quarter is now a single book of fragments, and even remembering it goes page by page.
The story here can't be laid out; it can only be replayed one room at a time, at its own pace.
node.N3-7.text:
Beyond the corridor lies a plaza so white it glows. Here the revocation lifted its pen, like a sentence that forgot its ending halfway through.
You sit down, bandage up, grind ink and copy out your scattered clues again.
When you look up, the view has opened out — from here, the story can finally be laid out flat. The Tide Tower stands on the horizon, a blank page at its top.
node.N4-1.text:
At the top of the Tide Tower's spiral stair, the last page hangs between the pendulums, white as a sea with no moon.
An old Scriptorium guard bars the page with his pen: no one touches this page.
Show him the signet and he'll let you pass; without it, the Inktide Avatar is waiting behind the page — and it remembers everyone who showed it mercy.
node.N4-1b.text:
Without the signet, the guard's pen comes down — and where its point lands, the Inktide Avatar rises from the back of the last page.
It is a tide made of every word Ashenport has lost, rolling half the city's names along with it.
As the crest bears down you think: either you outwrite it, or it copies you away.
node.N4-2.text:
The inktide drains away, and the last page settles quietly into your hands. Light as a breath, heavy as a whole city.
Mend it, and Ashenport returns to the Weave, at the cost of someone staying blank forever; burn it, and Ashenport is free, at the cost of slowly coming apart; or — with the fragments as your guide, take up the pen and write a new page.
Below the tower, the tide waits for your answer.
node.R1.text:
The first room is a home. The soup on the table still holds the shape of a spoonful being lifted, but the spoon is gone.
The name on the house plate has faded to an outline. You trace it with a fingertip — whoever lived here wrote their days full.
node.R2.text:
The second room is a classroom. The sums on the blackboard are half erased, and a child is crouching under the teacher's desk.
The whole quarter has been revoked, but he still remembers his own name — and because he "remembers", he's caught in a crack in the revocation.
You kneel and coax him, gently, to give you his hand. Catch it and he can be written back; miss, and this page can only be turned.
node.R3.text:
The third room has no walls — the Ink Fiends ate them.
Warped letters are stacked layer on layer in the dark; the whole nest is a ruined draft, and you are the only clean sentence on it.
They can smell the blank.
node.R4-r.text:
The first pack of Ink Fiends on the right drops from the lintel upside down, like a row of misplaced punctuation.
There's no time to rest here — another fight is waiting deeper in. Finish it fast, and keep moving.
node.R4-r2.text:
Deep inside is the nest's court: on a throne heaped from letters sit the oldest strokes among the Ink Fiends.
Once they were revoked street names, deleted love letters, last words that were crossed out. Now all they want is to file you away in the ruins too.
node.R4.text:
Ahead, the corridor splits left and right. Over the left-hand door is a line of small print only a Black Feather Token holder can read; the right-hand way stands open, and from its depths comes the sound of words chewing on words.
Kelan asks which way. You touch the token inside your coat — or just make a fist.
node.R5.text:
At the end of the corridor, the scribing golem the Scriptorium left behind is still on duty — the city has been revoked, and it's still copying.
Its pen drips gold ink, and its programming has no word for "stop": under its palm is the last Weaver's Fragment, copied over and over again.
Make it stop. That page should be kept by the living.

nodes.N3-1.edges.0.label: Push open the first door
nodes.N3-1.summary: The revoked old quarter survives only as fragments, replayed one room at a time.
nodes.N3-1.text_variants.0.text: You've read the Salvage Guild's ledger: they numbered the pages of this fragment long ago. You know which page to walk in through.
nodes.N3-1.title: Into the Revoked Quarter

nodes.N3-7.title: The Blank Plaza
nodes.N4-1.edges.0.label: Show the Scriptorium Signet and talk the guard down
nodes.N4-1.summary: A guard bars the way to the last page. The Signet may persuade him; otherwise the Inktide Avatar waits.
nodes.N4-1.text_variants.0.text: Someone is missing at the top of the stairs. The tax collector should have been here to testify — but you tore out his page yourself, and not even the guard can remember his name.
nodes.N4-1.title: Top of the Tide Tower
nodes.N4-1b.edges.0.label: Face the choice

nodes.R2.summary: A child who still remembers his own name.
nodes.R2.text_variants.0.text: You saw the ink fade at the pier, and you know which moment to catch — the child's fingertips haven't faded through yet, and you recognise the edge before he does.

nodes.N1-1m.title: The Fog Coast Road
nodes.N1-1m.summary: East of the plaza, sea fog crawls up the rocks. Choose a route and a pace, and roll for every stretch of road — each one costs time.
nodes.N1-1m.edges.0.label: Back to the plaza
nodes.N1-1mr.title: Fishers' Row
nodes.N1-1mr.summary: Half the house signs on the lane have faded to blank paper. An old fisherwoman squats in a doorway mending a net, its mesh thinner than the ink.
nodes.N1-1mr.edges.0.label: Help her mend the net
nodes.N1-1mr.edges.1.label: Back to the coast road
nodes.N1-1mc.title: Chapel of the Sunken Bell
nodes.N1-1mc.summary: The bell tower stands half under the tide. At low water you can see an offering box pinned under the bell's mouth.
nodes.N1-1mc.edges.0.label: Take the box from under the bell
nodes.N1-1mc.edges.1.label: Back to the coast road
nodes.N1-1ms.title: Salt Marsh
nodes.N1-1ms.summary: With the lighthouse lit again, a salt marsh shows through the fog. The salt crystals glint like unfinished words.
nodes.N1-1ms.edges.0.label: Gather salt crystals
nodes.N1-1ms.edges.1.label: Back to the coast road

sites.lighthouse.areas.3.text: The great lens is filmed with ink. The wick is still there; it only needs a flame.
